A few important considerations:

- The built-in TT-30 outlet provides approximately 20A of usable power, not the full 30A service.
- A 5,000 BTU air conditioner can consume 400–600W continuously, draining a 2kWh battery in just a few hours.
- If your RV refrigerator supports propane, use propane to conserve battery capacity.
- When connecting through the RV's electrical panel, use the proper transfer-switch arrangement. Turn off the converter once your RV house battery is fully charged. <Cite refs={["turn134047view0"]}/>

Remember that you typically get around 85% of the advertised battery capacity as usable AC energy after inverter losses.
